title: Fold a sedan's rear seatback from the trunk: one hand holds the spring-return knob, the other tips 9 kg past upright
instruction: Pull and hold the seatback lock knob in the trunk, push the rear seatback forward past upright, and let it fold down onto the seat cushion.
context: When a load is too long for a sedan's trunk, the driver folds a rear seatback down. The trunk is built full scale (floor, walls, arches, sill, opening flanges, shelf, all colliding). The arms work from inside the trunk; their bases stand on its floor, 65 cm in from the sill. Kia's 2024 Forte manual gives the purpose of folding: "to allow you to carry longer objects than could not otherwise be accommodated" (t00042), and the step: "Pull out the seatback locking knob(1) in the trunk, then fold the seat toward the front of the vehicle" (t00043). Hyundai's 2010 Elantra manual has a seatback locking knob in the trunk too. In this task's latch model, the knob springs back, and let go before the seatback leaves its striker, the latch catches again, so one hand holds it while the other pushes. The seatback, 9 kg reclined 25 degrees, is pushed past upright and gravity folds it.
setup: The arms work from inside the trunk; their bases stand on its floor, 65 cm in from the sill. Positions in cm from the midpoint between the arm bases, which are bolted to the floor at y 30.5 and -30.5 (README, Arm bases): x forward toward the seat, y to the robot's left, heights above the trunk floor; the hinge is 1.25 m from the sill. (1) The trunk of a 2019-2021 Kia Forte sedan at full scale, all fixed: carpeted floor from the sill (x -65) to the seatback foot (x 55); side walls at y 49.5 and -85.5 (1.35 m apart), 60 cm tall up to the parcel shelf; a wheel arch at each wall, 28 cm tall and 7.5 cm deep, x 7.5 to 57.5 (1.20 m between the arches); the sill, 12 cm tall, x -71 to -65; the opening's side flanges, 10 cm in from each wall, x -65 to -50; the parcel shelf, underside at height 60, x 5 to 27 (the shelf collides whole and is drawn as its two edges; the real trial uses an opaque board); the opening, sill to shelf, 70 cm long and 1.15 m wide. Sizes and their sources: README, Sizes and Trunk. (2) The 40% rear seatback (bought as Kia part 89300M7330B4U, with its latch, knob, cable and striker; the buyer checks that it is the 40% section): 55 wide (y -20.5 to 34.5), 60 tall, 10 thick, 9 kg, hinged at its foot at x 60, height 6, reclined 25 degrees toward the robot, its top at about x 30, height 60; outboard headrest lowered, fixed to it. The 60% seatback stands latched beside it (y -85.5 to -22). (3) The rear cushion top, a plate 54 x 55 x 1.2 cm, x 66 to 120, under where the seatback folds (the cushion beside it is drawn, 11 cm tall); the folded stop is the recline plus 88, 113 degrees of swing. (4) A striker latch at the seatback's top corner holds it at the start. (5) The seatback lock knob, a flat pull tab 25 mm tall, 12 mm thick and 15 mm long on a 10 mm rod, on the trunk-side trim beside the seatback top (trim x 34.5 to 40.5, y 36 to 49.5, height 40 to 62, against the left wall), its face at x 32, y 44.5, height 52, 8 cm below the height of the shelf's underside and 5 cm from the left wall; it pulls 20 mm toward the robot against a return spring of about 7 N at full pull. In this task's latch model, the knob springs back, and let go before the seatback leaves its striker, the latch catches again, so one hand holds it while the other pushes. The latch is free while the knob is pulled 15 mm or more; the seatback is off the striker at 5 degrees of swing. The push is 34 N static (51.7 N peak in the demo); the bench check tests the arm's push before a run counts (README, Bench checks).
scoring: Judged on the hinge angle (0 when latched) at the end; stop when folded and at rest for 1.0 s, or at 60 s: the run ends at the first step with the full score (real trial: digital angle gauge on the seatback, 0.1 degree, and a 30 fps film from the cabin side). Off the striker: swung 5 degrees or more, which needs the latch released (0.33). Past upright: swung more than the recline, 25 degrees (0.67). Folded and at rest: every step of the last 1.0 s within 10 degrees of the folded stop (113 degrees of swing at the 25-degree recline, so 103 or more) and the angle moving 1.0 degree or less in all (1.0). By geometry, in every pose found the gripper point nearest the folded seatback is at its foot; 288 simulator runs on 242 poses: 0 held it (README, Both hands).
reset_notes: About 30 s, nothing consumed: lift the seatback by its top and push it back, holding it, until the latch clicks; check that the knob has sprung back. No hidden variables; no seed changes the scene.
fidelity: Full scale; sizes are estimates. Both ends of 8-11 kg, recline 23-28 deg, spring 5-10 N, release 10-19 mm, striker 3-7 deg, run together: 1.0. Shelf 50-61 cm (at 50 a fingertip touches it), left wall 3-20 cm, knob 2 cm in depth, height (place read from scene): 1.0. Latch is a joint lock freed at 15 of 20 mm pull: a hand must still hold the sprung knob. Seatback is rigid: its 9 kg sets the push. Shelf is drawn as two bars: it collides whole. Arms stand on the trunk floor: one holds, one pushes.
scores: Scripted demo 1.0 at step 216 (10.8 s), on an RTX 3090 Ti and an RTX 4070 Ti SUPER. No action, push without the release, pull without a push, pull then let go, hard shove: 0.0 each. Stopped at 109.9 degrees before rest: 0.667. Dream-1: 0.0 (1,200 steps); valid, one session, 0 errored trials.
